data.turoyo: I čamkayo, d kətyo b iḏe du mḥalqono, yaʕni du məštaʕyono, ham komḥaləq u pallo w kəmčalqazle w ham ste komakili i maṣafa, d bayn lu pallo w li ḥəlle eba, yaʕni koḥəzyo a tlaṯ waḏ̣ifatani.
data.translation: Das Schlagholz, das in der Hand des Schleuderers ist, der gerade am Spiel ist, dient also zu drei zwecken: Er schleudert damit das Flugholz, er pariert es in der Luft, und man mißt damit den Abstand zwischen Flugholz und Freistau ab.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; explanation gives the instrument and distinguishes its three functions.

data.turoyo: W iḏa d ḥa m an naʕimanək, heš i qarno lalʕal, meqəm me d nəḥto li arʕo, d mčalqazla, disa kəppe moḥəlla.
data.translation: Wenn nachdem taʕmîj einer von den Jungen sie in der Luft schlägt, ehe sie noch auf die Erde herabgekommen ist, so dürfen sie wieder schlagen.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; feminine object and positive conditional rule.

data.turoyo: W haka d nošo m am məštaʕyone, i naqqa d kəmḥaləq i qarno w i naqqa d komər “šoriṭ”, d nošo lo mčalqazla, nošo laybe moḥela. <...>
data.translation: Und wenn keiner von den Spielern, nachdem er das Horn geworfen und schōrît gesagt hat, es in der Luft pariert, so darf keiner es mehr schlagen. <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; explicit negation and the contrasting horn-game rule.

summary: All five occurrences describe striking/intercepting a flying game piece and fit I.1. The contexts concern tipcat and a horn; the object change does not justify another technical sense.
Infectum occurs with an indicative prefix, a conditional d-clause and negation. -le refers to the tipcat and -la to the horn; mčalqzalle in 94/515 is the completed Preterit within a temporal clause.

The existing 94/383 and 94/515 quotations already represent two of the records. Add the stick-function explanation and positive/negative conditional rules without repeating those inherited quotations.

The inherited figurative gloss is preserved, but none of these records independently attests forestalling an attack. Unknown etymology cannot be resolved from this sample. No light-verb collocation is present.
Seek an independent corpus example of the inherited figurative attack-prevention use; it is not attested in these five game descriptions.
Is the technical action best described as striking away or intercepting in the air? The source gloss and translations support both descriptions; no new sense is inferred.
Correct the case governed by German abwehren
rationale: Abwehren takes an accusative object: einen Angriff abwehren. The existing einem is a dative ending in an otherwise accusative construction; the later dative ihm belongs to zuvorkommt and remains correct.
